The commented intent ('any property with a number is the expiry') is not implemented: Salesforce's refreshed credential is persisted without `instance_url` (its next jsforce.Connection cannot reach the API), and Office365's spread `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` now contributes only access_token, so the stored expiry is never advanced and every subsequent call re-triggers a sync-endpoint refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Both expressions evaluate to a runtime string key (effectively `"[object Object]"`), so one overwrites the other and they do not create a real “any string key” constraint. Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, in sync-mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the safe-parse result’s `.data` will include essentially only the explicitly declared keys (not arbitrary fields like `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.). The diff shows downstream code relying on these fields: Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (so expiry may not advance), and Salesforce persists `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ...}` (so `instance_url` can be dropped), matching the finding’s reported broken behavior.
